parts.prompt_markdown: Use a suitable approximating distribution to calculate \(P(X \leq 150)\).
Justify the use of your approximating distribution in this case.

skills: Select an appropriate approximation to the Poisson distribution for the given range
Compute P(X≤150) using the approximation
Justify why the approximation is suitable
methods: Poisson-to-normal (or other suitable) approximation to the CDF
Continuity correction (if used)
Justification via comparison of assumptions (e.g., sufficiently large mean, tail not too extreme)
subtopics: Approximating a Poisson CDF (e.g., normal approximation)
Using an approximation and checking its validity

parts.prompt_markdown: Use Henri's digits to find the numbers of the next two students in the sample.
Use this information to calculate an unbiased estimate of the mean of \(X\) and show that an unbiased estimate of the variance of \(X\) is less than 0.1.
Henri's friend claims that Henri has probably made a mistake in his calculation of \(\Sigma x\) or \(\Sigma x^2\). Use your answer to part (b) to comment on this claim.

skills: Generate the next two random-number-based student indices
Compute an unbiased estimator of the population mean from sample data
Compute an unbiased estimator of the variance and compare it to 0.1
Use estimates to assess whether earlier arithmetic could be mistaken
methods: Random-number sampling using provided digits
Method of moments with known n, Σx, Σx²
Unbiased estimators: mean = x̄ and variance = (Σx²−n x̄²)/(n−1)
Bounding/inequality comparison against 0.1 using computed value
subtopics: Unbiased estimation of mean and variance from sample moments
Using sample sums to compute estimators

questions.stem_markdown:
Henri wants to choose a random sample from the 804 students at his college. He numbers the students from 1 to 804 and then uses random numbers generated by his calculator. The first 20 random digits produced by his calculator are as follows.

5 6 7 1 0 9 8 4 3 1 0 9 6 6 5 0 2 1 7 6

Henri's first two student numbers are 567 and 109.

There were 30 students in Henri's sample. He asked each of them how much time, \(X\) hours, they spent on social media each week, on average. He summarised the results as follows.

\[
n = 30 \quad \Sigma x = 610 \quad \Sigma x^2 = 12405
\]

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: B1 for each. Allow 021. If more than 2 **answers** given, count first two and ISW.
OE or 20.3.
Use of correct formula.
Accept $$\frac{5}{87}$$.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Variance is [unrealistically] small so Henri has [probably] made a mistake/claim is [probably] correct
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Need both parts. Need ‘small’ OE, not just < 0.1. FT *their* < 0.1 variance value (not –ve), e.g. 0.0556 (if omit $$\frac{30}{29}$$). Accept ‘s.d. = 0.24 is small, so Henri has probably made a mistake’. Note: ‘mean is large/small’ scores B0, but ‘mean large compared to variance so Henri prob made a mistake’ scores B1.

skills: Relate the reported lower confidence limit to the standard error
Extract α from the confidence level used to form the interval

methods: Compute p-hat from the sample
Use CI form p̂ ± z_{α/2}√(p̂(1−p̂)/n)
Solve for z_{α/2} from the given lower limit then find α
subtopics: Determining confidence level from an interval bound

questions.stem_markdown:
A student wishes to estimate the proportion, \(p\), of students at her college who have exactly one brother. She surveys a random sample of 50 students at her college and finds that 18 of them have exactly one brother. She calculates an approximate \(\alpha\%\) confidence interval for \(p\) and finds that the lower limit of the confidence interval is \(0.244\) correct to 3 significant figures.

Find \(\alpha\) correct to the nearest integer. [4]

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Use of correct equation.
Accept 1.71 if nothing better seen.
Attempt area above or below their 1.709 and use correct method to find $$\alpha$$.
Allow $$\alpha = 91\%$$ 0.91 or 91.2 score A0.

parts.prompt_markdown: Find the probability that, in a randomly chosen match, the team scores at least 5 goals.

questions.stem_markdown: The number of goals scored by a sports team in the first half of any match has the distribution \(X \sim Po(3.1)\). The number of goals scored by the same team in the second half of any match has the distribution \(Y \sim Po(2.4)\). You may assume that the distributions of \(X\) and \(Y\) are independent.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Condone one end error. Any $$\lambda$$. Accept fully correct $$\Sigma$$ notation. Expression must be seen.
Correct answer with no working scores **SC B1**.
SOI
Condone one end error. Any $$\lambda$$. Accept fully correct $$\Sigma$$ notation. Expression must be seen.
Correct answer with no working scores **SC B1 B1**.
Find P(3 in first half AND 2 in second half). Must see expression.
Use of 5.5 to find P(5).

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: $$P(P(\text{exactly } 3 \text{ in } 1^{\text{st}} \text{ half given total } 5) = \frac{P(\text{exactly } 3 \text{ in } 1^{\text{st}} \text{ half and total } 5)}{P(\text{total } 5)}$$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Attempt at conditional probability; numerator = *their* 0.05844 and denominator = P(total 5) Note: $$(\frac{3.1^3}{3!} \times \frac{2.4^2}{2!}) \div (\frac{5.5^4}{5!})$$ scores M1 M1 M1.

parts.prompt_markdown: Test at the 2.5% significance level whether the mean mass of cereal boxes filled by the machine has decreased.

Later the inspector carries out a similar test at the 2.5% significance level, using the same hypotheses and another 120 randomly chosen cereal boxes.

Given that the mean mass is now actually 506 grams, find the probability of a Type II error.

skills: Formulate hypotheses for decreased mean
Compute test statistic and p-value/critical region at 2.5% significance level
Given the true mean, compute probability of failing to reject (Type II error)
methods: Z-test with known population standard deviation: (x̄−μ0)/(σ/√n)
One-sided rejection region at significance level 0.025
Type II error β = P(fail to reject | true mean = 506) = Φ((z_crit−(μ1−μ0)/SE))
subtopics: One-sample z-test for mean with known σ
Two-sided vs one-sided specification via hypotheses

questions.stem_markdown:
The masses of cereal boxes filled by a certain machine have mean 510 grams. An adjustment is made to the machine and an inspector wishes to test whether the mean mass of cereal boxes filled by the machine has decreased.

After the adjustment is made, he chooses a random sample of 120 cereal boxes. The mean mass of these boxes is found to be 508 grams.

Assume that the standard deviation of the masses is 10 grams.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: H_{0}: Population mean mass = 510 g H_{1}: Population mean mass < 510 g
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Allow ‘μ’ but not just ‘mean’.
Standardising must have $$\sqrt{120}$$.
OE For valid comparison. Inequality sign the wrong way round scores M1 A0.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: [Reject H_{0}] There is sufficient evidence to suggest that the [mean] mass has decreased
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: OE In context (must be ‘decreased’ OE, not ‘changed’); not definite. No contradictions. Condone ‘there is sufficient evidence to support the inspector’s claim’. NB: Accept alternative method using critical value (= 508.21) and comparison with 508. Condone 509.79 compared with 510. Two tail test scores maximum B0 M1 A1 M1 A0; must have comparison with 0.0125 or 2.24/2.241.
Standardising to find critical value (must use 510 and $$10 \div \sqrt{120}$$). Accept $$\pm 1.96$$.
Accept 3 sf if nothing better seen. Note: cv could be found in **(a)**.
Standardising with their 508.21 and 506 (must use $$10 \div \sqrt{120}$$).
For area consistent with their working.
Note: $$\frac{510 - 506}{10 \div \sqrt{120}}$$ scores max M0 A0 M1 M1 A0.

questions.stem_markdown:
The probability density function, \(f\), of a random variable \(X\) is given by

\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}
k(1+\cos x) & 0\leq x\leq \pi,\\
0 & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]

where \(k\) is a constant.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Attempt integrate $$f(x)$$ with correct limits and equate to 1.
Correct integration.
AG Some evidence of substitution of limits, i.e. at least one interim step (e.g. $$k\pi = 1$$) as minimum requirement. Convincingly obtained; no errors seen.

Substitute correct limits into their integral. OR_{1}: integrate 0 to 0.83 and 0.84 to $$\pi$$. OR_{2}: use g(m) = m + sin m - ($$\pi/2$$) and find g(0.83) and g(0.84). OR_{3}: use h(m) = m + sin m and find h(0.83) and h(0.84). Both attempted.

FT their areas; dep 0.5 is between their areas OE. OR_{1}: 0.499 < 0.5 and 0.496 < 0.5, so 0.83 < m < 0.84. OR_{2}: g(0.83) > 0 g(0.84) < 0 OE, so 0.83 < m < 0.84. OR_{3}: h(0.83) < $$\frac{\pi}{2}$$ h(0.84) > $$\frac{\pi}{2}$$, so 0.83 < m < 0.84. Both statements needed. Note: A score of M1 A0 A1FT is possible.
Attempt integrate $$x f(x)$$. Ignore limits.

OE Attempt to integrate (using ‘parts’) with correct limits, reaching an expression of the form $$ax^2 + uv - \int v du$$. OR using parts to integrate $$x(1+\cos x)$$ reaching an expression of the form $$uv - \int v du$$ i.e. $$\frac{1}{\pi} (x^2 + x \sin x - \int (x + \sin x) dx)$$

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: $$= \frac{1}{\pi} \left( \frac{x^2}{2} + x \sin x + \cos x \right)$$ or e.g. $$\frac{\pi}{2} + \frac{1}{\pi} (0 - [-\cos x]_0^\pi)$$ or e.g. $$\frac{\pi}{2} + \frac{1}{\pi} ((-1 - 1))$$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Integration fully correct.
OE ISW after correct exact value seen. **SC1:** Unsupported answer of $$\frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{2}{\pi}$$ scores **B3**. **SC2:** Unsupported answer of 0.934 scores **B2**.
